parties:
Paradise Metallurgical Complex ltd
Vs.
Superintendent Customs, Excise & Vat Fatullah Circle Narayanganj and Others
full_judgment: 8. The learned Advocate for the Petitioner Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud by referring to the Petitioner's representation of 31.12.2003, as admittedly and evidently received by the office of the Respondent No. 3 Deputy Commissioner, Customs, Exercise and VAT on the same date (Annexure-'J'), submits that the VAT Authority acted in disregard of the duty under Section 9(2kha) to substantively dispose of the objection raised in the representation of December, 2003 within the seven working-day period prescribed therein. That dereliction of duty, Mr. Mahmud submits, has resulted in the objections so raised by the Petitioner prevailing over the impugned cancellation of rebate and the impugned detection and adjustment consequentially staying in the books merely as an inconclusive decision. It is argued that in light of the representation made on 31.12.2003 it was incumbent upon the VAT Authority to conclusively decide upon the matter upon a due and fair determination of the issues raised in objection upon the Petitioner being given an opportunity to be heard. That, according to Mr. Mahmud, is the clear prescription of Section 9(2kha), and the due fulfillment and compliance with which is the absolute prerequisite for any decision made under the said Section to attain finality. This Court notes that admittedly no decision whatsoever, let alone a conclusive decision, under Section 9(2kha) disposing of the Petitioner's objection has yet been made. Unarguably, the time to arrive at a conclusive, effective and final decision, i.e., the statutory seven working-day period clearly prescribed in Section 9 (2kha), has in the meantime also long since elapsed. Referring to the Writ Petition itself, Mr. Mahmud submits that the Respondents may thereafter still have had recourse to the procedure under Section 55 of the Act for recovery of tax due subject, however, to notice issued for recovery of same within five years from the date on which such sum fell due. Clearly, however, the Respondents did not embark upon that course of action either and, in any case, are now barred by the statutory period of limitation from proceeding so against the Petitioner. Furthermore, the spectre of fraud or deception as raised by the Respondent No. 3 in the Affidavit-in-Opposition, Mr. Mahmud states, is one that the Respondents had not raised either in their earlier dealings with the Petitioner in general or most notably in the communication of 26.10.2003 (Annexure-`G') which placed the Petitioner otherwise on notice of an imminent inspection of its premises under Section 26 of the Act.
